## 10-Pin Bowling for Commodore 64: Strike!

Step up to the lanes in *10-Pin Bowling* for the Commodore 64! Experience the thrill of classic bowling from a unique, slightly elevated perspective, looking out from behind your bowler. Fine-tune your game with precise left-to-right positioning before each throw.  Adjust the camera angle with the + and - keys and choose your dominant hand (right or left) for a truly personalized bowling experience.

Master the art of the release – move the joystick forward and press the fire button to send your ball hurtling down the lane.  Be mindful of your approach; moving too far forward results in a foul! The game automatically calculates scores, striving for that elusive perfect 300.  Whether you're a seasoned pro or a casual bowler, *10-Pin Bowling* offers accessible yet engaging gameplay, perfect for honing your skills and competing for the highest score.  Get ready to roll!

The Commodore 64, affectionately known as the C64, was an 8-bit home computer released in 1982 that became a cultural icon and the best-selling desktop computer of all time, with estimated sales between 12.5 and 17 million units. Boasting 64 kilobytes of RAM and impressive graphics and sound capabilities thanks to its VIC-II chip and SID sound chip, the C64 offered a significant leap in performance compared to its predecessors. It initially sold for $595, but its price later dropped, making it accessible to a wider audience.

The C64 dominated the home computer market throughout the 1980s, particularly in the US and UK, though it faced stiff competition from the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC. Popular games like *Impossible Mission*, *The Last Ninja*, and *Elite* showcased its capabilities and cemented its legacy. Even today, emulators allow enthusiasts to relive the C64 experience.
